subject: Data subject request: access & deletion for user 43f2 — evidence package timeline
messages:
From: Lisa Hart <lisa.hart@acmecorp.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-legal@acmecorp.com
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Data subject request — access and deletion for user id 43f2

Hi Irene,

We are raising a formal data subject request under our DPA and GDPR for one of our end users (internal id: 43f2). The user has requested (1) a full copy of personal data you store/process related to them, and (2) deletion of all personal data where we (Acme) are the controller and Redwood acts as a processor.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood is acting as controller or processor for data collected by the Hosted API for our account (acme-prod) and for any telemetry/usage logs.
- A proposed timeline for producing an evidence package (access export + provenance + processing operations) and for completing deletion where applicable.
- Whether SCCs are in place and effective for cross-border transfers for our account, and if you can share the relevant reference or confirmation statement.

Per our DPA, we expect initial evidence within 10 business days. Please let us know if you require further detail from the requesting user (proof of identity), or if we should provide a consent/authorization form.

I have attached the signed proof request from the user.

Thanks,
Lisa
Lisa Hart
Senior Counsel, Privacy — Acme Corp
lisa.hart@acmecorp.com

Attachment: dsr-proof-request.pdf
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Hart <lisa.hart@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data subject request — access and deletion for user id 43f2

Hi Lisa — thanks for the note and for attaching the user's proof. We're assigning this a privacy ticket and will follow our DSR workflow. A few quick clarifying items so we can scope the package accurately:

- Can you confirm the exact date range to include in the access export (we typically pull the last 24 months by default unless you specify otherwise).
- Does Acme want the full request exported in raw JSON (API payloads + metadata) or a redacted CSV summary for user-facing copy? We can provide both; the raw export requires additional authorization steps.
- For deletion: do you want logical deletion only (remove from application indexes) or evidence of complete removal from backups/archives to the extent Redwood controls them? Note that backups are on a standard rotation; we will include deletion plan and estimated complete date.

To confirm roles briefly: for Hosted API requests (acme-prod), Redwood acts as processor per our standard DPA; for telemetry/operational logs we may be controller for platform monitoring — we'll surface the exact mapping in writing.

I'm cc'ing Marissa (privacy ops) and Markus (Head of Compliance) to pull the export and assemble the evidence package. We will produce an initial package (redacted access export + processing log + SCC reference) within 7 business days and follow up on deletion scope within 10 business days. If that timeline is problematic, please let us know.

Regards,
Irene
Irene Choi
Privacy & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: internal-dsr-routing.md (internal checklist)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Hart <lisa.hart@acmecorp.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data subject request — access and deletion for user id 43f2

Hi Lisa / Irene,

I've started assembling the evidence package and wanted to outline what we'll include and requested next steps from Acme to avoid delays. This follows our DSR playbook but I'm listing specifics so you can confirm.

Planned deliverables (initial package):
- Access export (redacted CSV) covering last 24 months unless Acme specifies a different range. Columns: timestamp, event_type, resource_id, processed_payload_summary.
- Processing ops log for the account (service nodes involved, regions, timestamps of processing).
- Copy of applicable SCC clause statement and link to execution record (we'll supply the SCC appendix id).
- Explanation of Redwood's role mapping for acme-prod: processor for API request payloads; controller for platform usage telemetry (short explanation and examples).
- Audit trail showing when request data was created/updated and who (service) accessed it.

Deletion scope and options:
- Logical deletion from active indices and customer-visible APIs: typical completion = 3 business days post-approval.
- Removal from snapshot backups: best-effort removal upon next backup cycle; we will provide the retention window and expected date. Redwood does not guarantee immediate eradication from immutable backups outside scheduled retention windows unless an enterprise contract amendment is in place.

What we need from Acme to proceed:
1) Confirm date range for export (default: 2024-11-30 to 2026-11-30).
2) Confirm whether to include raw API payload JSON in the package (requires signed authorization).
3) Confirm deletion preference: logical-only or request backup purge (and whether you'd like an attestation when completed).

Attachments to our reply packet: dsr-evidence-package-template.pdf (template outline), access-log-export-43f2.csv (sample extract placeholder). We'll replace placeholders with the full export once the range and raw/redacted preference are confirmed.

Quoted for context:
> On Sun, 29 Nov 2026 at 15:12, Lisa Hart <lisa.hart@acmecorp.com> wrote:
> > We are raising a formal data subject request under our DPA and GDPR for one of our end users (internal id: 43f2)...

Next steps: please reply to this thread with the three confirmations above. Once we have them, we'll generate the full export and a deletion plan timeline.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Privacy Operations Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments: dsr-evidence-package-template.pdf, access-log-export-43f2.csv
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data subject request — access and deletion for user id 43f2

Hi Lisa — thanks for the quick review. Per Marissa's checklist, here's what we will do and the expected timeline once you confirm the three items:

- Initial evidence package (redacted CSV export + processing ops summary + SCC confirmation): available within 5 business days after confirmation.
- Logical deletion from active indices and APIs: completion within 3 business days after approval to delete.
- Backup/snapshot removal: we will provide the retention window and target date for purge; if you require expedited removal from backups, let us know so we can raise with Infrastructure and provide an attestation where feasible.

A few clarifications on controller/processor: Redwood is a processor for request payloads submitted by Acme via the Hosted API (we process on your behalf per the DPA). However, certain operational telemetry (e.g., node-level metrics, internal error logs) are collected for platform health and may be processed as controller data; Marissa will include explicit mapping and examples in the package so you can reconcile with your internal records.

We've created a secure shared folder for the packet: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/Acme/DSR-43f2 (link expires in 14 days). Please upload the signed authorization if you want raw JSON included; otherwise confirm the date range and deletion preference and we'll proceed.

If everything looks good, we'll plan the initial delivery by EOD next Friday (2026-12-04 PST).

Best,
Irene Choi
